name: Shen Men
location: In the triangular fossa, toward its upper-central region.
traditionalUse: Commonly selected in auricular wellness routines intended to promote calm and overall balance.
howToStimulate: Press gently for 5–10 seconds, release, and repeat a few times. Stop if the area becomes painful or irritated.

name: Point Zero
location: Near the center of the ear, around the root of the helix.
traditionalUse: Often used as a balancing or centering point in auricular practice.
howToStimulate: Use light, steady pressure. More pressure is not necessarily better.

name: Heart
traditionalUse: Traditionally included in routines related to calm, rest and emotional settling.
howToStimulate: Press gently and discontinue use if you notice persistent tenderness or skin irritation.

name: Sympathetic
location: Near the junction of the inferior crus of the antihelix and the inner helix.
traditionalUse: Frequently included in traditional comfort and relaxation combinations.
howToStimulate: Apply brief, comfortable pressure several times through the day.

name: Kidney
traditionalUse: Traditionally associated with foundational energy and restorative routines.
howToStimulate: Use gentle pressure only and keep the surrounding skin clean and dry.

name: Occiput
location: On the posterior-superior area of the antitragus.
traditionalUse: Commonly referenced in routines for rest and head comfort.
howToStimulate: Press until you feel mild pressure, not sharp pain.

name: Stomach
location: Around the end of the crus of the helix in the concha.
traditionalUse: Traditionally included in digestive-support and appetite-awareness routines.
howToStimulate: Stimulate gently before or after meals as part of a mindful routine.

name: Spleen
location: In the concha region, close to the liver and stomach representations.
traditionalUse: Traditionally linked with digestive and energy-support routines.
howToStimulate: Use light pressure and avoid applying seeds to broken or inflamed skin.

name: Brain
location: On the inner aspect of the antitragus.
traditionalUse: Often selected in traditional routines for clarity, rest and general regulation.
howToStimulate: Press comfortably for a few seconds at a time.

name: Endocrine
location: At the base of the intertragic notch.
traditionalUse: Traditionally included in women’s wellness and general regulation routines.
howToStimulate: Apply light pressure only. Seek professional guidance for persistent symptoms.

name: Mouth
location: Near the lower portion of the concha, close to the ear canal opening.
traditionalUse: Sometimes used in mindful-eating and oral-comfort routines.
howToStimulate: Press gently and keep seeds away from the ear canal.

name: Cervical Spine
location: Along the lower antihelix, corresponding traditionally to the neck region.
howToStimulate: Use comfortable pressure and seek medical care for severe, persistent or injury-related pain.

name: Shoulder
location: Along the antihelix region traditionally corresponding to the shoulder.
howToStimulate: Press gently. Do not use ear seeds as a substitute for assessment after injury.

name: Jaw
location: On the earlobe region traditionally mapped to the jaw and face.
howToStimulate: Use mild pressure and consult a dental or medical professional for persistent jaw pain.
